questions.q: In an LC oscillator, if values of inductance and capacitance become twice and eight times, respectively, then the resonant frequency of oscillator becomes <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> times its initial resonant frequency <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>ω</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Resonance frequency of an LC oscillations circuit is stated as 

ω0=1LC, here, L and C represents inductance and capacitance of circuit.

Now, when inductance and capacitance changes, i.e., L'=2L and C'=8C

Then, resonant frequency is ω=12L×8C=14LC

⇒ω=ω04

Thus, the value of x=14.

questions.q: If wattless current flows in the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>AC</mi></math> circuit, then the circuit is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: The current in an AC circuit containing only either a capacitor or an inductor is said to be wattless as the average power is zero. As wattless current has phase difference of ϕ=90° with voltage, therefore power factor cosϕ will be zero.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : Choke coil is simply a coil having a large inductance but a small resistance. Choke coils are used with fluorescent mercury-tube fittings. If household electric power is directly connected to a mercury tube, the tube will be damaged.
Reason (R): By using the choke coil, the voltage across the tube is reduced by a factor \(\left(R / \sqrt{R^2+\omega^2 L^2}\right)\), where \(\omega\) is frequency of the supply across resistor \(R\) and inductor L . If the choke coil were not used, the voltage across the resistor would be the same as the applied voltage.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both \((\mathbf{A})\) and \((\mathbf{R})\) are true but \((\mathbf{R})\) is not the correct explanation of \((\mathbf{A})\)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $I=\frac{V}{\sqrt{R^2+\omega^2 L^2}}V_R=\frac{R}{\sqrt{R^2+\omega^2 L^2}} V$

questions.q: In the figure shown, a circuit contains two identical resistors with resistance R=5 Ω and an inductance with L=2 mH. An ideal battery of 15V is connected in the circuit. What will be the current through the battery long after the switch is closed?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
After a long time, when the growth of current in the circuit has stopped, the inductor will work as a conductor. Therefore the effective resistance of the circuit will be, 

R=52=2.5 Ω

Hence, the current through the circuit will be,

I=VR=152.5=6A

The average power dissipated in one cycle is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Standard expression of voltage is given by, V=V0sinωt and for current is given by, I=I0sinωt+ϕ. Clearly, ϕ is the phase difference here. From the given expression, ϕ=π3.

Average power dissipated in one cycle is given by,

 Pavg=VrmsIrmscos(ϕ)

=1002×100×10-32×cosπ3

=1042×10-3×12

=104=2.5 W

questions.q: To increase the resonant frequency in series LCR circuit,
options: Another resistance should be added in series with the first resistance.
Another capacitor should be added in series with the first capacitor
The source frequency should be decreased
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The resonant frequency of an LCR circuit is given by f=12πLC. It does not depend on the source frequency as well as the resistance of the circuit.

Therefore, to increase the resonating frequency product of L and C should decrease.

By joining another capacitor in series, the equivalent capacitor will decrease.

Hence, option C is correct option.

=628×5×10-3

=3.14 Ω

questions.q: A resistance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>40</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi></math> is connected to a source of alternating current rated <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>220</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>50</mn><mo> </mo><mi>Hz</mi></math>. Find the time taken by the current to change from its maximum value to the rms value :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The current in AC is of the form of i=i0sinωt. The maximum current is i0 and rms current is i02. The change in the phase when current change from maximum to rms value is π4 rad. Therefore, the time taken for the same will be,

t=∆ϕω=π4×2π×50=2.5 ms.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I : When the frequency of an AC source in a series LCR circuit increases, the current in the circuit first increases, attains a maximum value and then decreases.

Statement II : In a series LCR circuit, the value of power factor at resonance is one.

In the light of given statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
When an a.c. voltage is applied in a series LCR circuit, the current is increased first, attains a maximum and then decreases.

The formula to calculate the power factor is given by

cosϕ=RR2+XL2-XC2   ...1

At resonance, XL=XC, Hence,

cosϕresonance=1

Thus, both the statements are true.

How long will the current take to reach the peak value starting from zero?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
If initial value of current is zero, then it will take T4 time to reach the peak value, where T= time period.

As we know, ω=120π

Therefore,

t=T4=2πω4 =π2ω=π2×120π=1240 s

questions.q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: In an LCR series circuit, current is maximum at resonance.
Statement II: Current in a purely resistive circuit can never be less than that in a series LCR circuit when connected to same voltage source.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct from the options given below:
options: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Statement-I $I_m=\frac{V_m}{\sqrt{R^2+\left(X_L-X_C\right)^2}}$ at resonance $X_L=X_C$ Thus, $I_m=\frac{V_m}{R}\because$ Impendence is minimum therefore $I$ is maximum at resonance.
Statement-II $\mathrm{I}=\left(\frac{\mathrm{V}}{\mathrm{R}}\right)$ in purely resistive circuit.

The formula for maximum current is given by 

Imax=ωCVm   ...(i)

The given data is 

ω=120π

Vm=36 VC=150 μF

Substituting the values in equation (i)

Imax=120π×150×10-6×36

=2.036 A

≈2 A

questions.q: In the given circuit, the magnitude of VL and VC are twice that of VR. Given that f=50 Hz, the inductance of the coil is 1 Kπ mH. The value of K is _____ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Since the voltage across the inductor and capacitor is same, the circuit is in resonance. Therefore, the current in the circuit will be,

i=VR=2205=44 A.

The voltage across the inductor is double that across the resistor. Therefore, VL=2VR=440 V.

We know that VL=iXL=i×2πfL⇒L=44044×100π=110π H=100πmH

Therefore, K=1100=0.01≈0.

questions.q: An inductor of reactance $100 \Omega$, a capacitor of reactance $50 \Omega$, and a resistor of resistance $50 \Omega$ are connected in series with an AC source of 10 V , 50 Hz. Average power dissipated by the circuit is ________ W.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{P}=\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{rms}} \mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{rms}} \cos \phi \\ & \mathrm{P}=\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{rms}} \times \frac{\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{rms}}}{\mathrm{z}} \times \frac{\mathrm{R}}{\mathrm{z}} \\ & \mathrm{P}=\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{rms}}^2 \times \frac{\mathrm{R}}{\mathrm{z}^2} \\ & \mathrm{z}=\sqrt{\mathrm{R}^2+\left(\mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{L}}-\mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{C}}\right)^2} \\ & \mathrm{Z}=50 \sqrt{2} \Omega \\ & \mathrm{P}=100 \times \frac{50}{2500 \times 2}=1 \mathrm{~W}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A series LCR circuit with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>L</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>100</mn><mi>π</mi></mfrac><mo> </mo><mi>mH</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><mi>π</mi></mfrac><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi></math>, is connected across an AC source of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>220</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>50</mn><mo> </mo><mi>Hz</mi></math> supply. The power factor of the circuit would be ____.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The capacitive reactance of the circuit is given by, 

Xc=1ωC=π2π×50×10-3=10 Ω

The inductive reactance of the circuit is given by, 

XL=ωL=2π×50×100π×10-3=10 Ω

From above calculations, it is clear that

XC=XL

∴ Power factor =RZ=RR=1

questions.q: An ideal transformer with purely resistive load operates at 12 kV on the primary side. It supplies electrical energy to a number of nearby houses at 120 V. The average rate of energy consumption in the houses served by the transformer is 60 kW. The value of resistive load (Rs) required in the secondary circuit will be_________mΩ.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The given data is 

P=60×103 W

Vs=120 V

A transformer has a primary coil and a secondary coil.

The formula for the power delivered is given by 

P=V2sRs

⇒60×103=120×120Rs⇒Rs=120×12060×103=240 mΩ
